The demand atlas:
niches, funders, and where we fit.

Every niche is a coordinate — a behavioural mechanism family × approach type — with funders and grants attached as evidence, never as the organising axis. 737 harvested grants across 80 funders, each traceable to a logged source URL, crossed against our own project database and evidence gap map to show where CSBC can credibly stand.

Overview

How to read this, in ninety seconds

This atlas reorganises the funder landscape the way we sell, not the way funders label themselves. A niche is one cell of the matrix: a behavioural mechanism family (trust calibration, norms, present bias…) crossed with an approach type (RCT, diagnostic, evaluation, capability building…). Sector — health, climate, education — is only a tag.

The three layers in every niche card

  • Demand evidence. Actual harvested grants in that cell — funder, recipient, year, amount where public, purpose, and a live source link for every row. This is who has funded what, verbatim from the harvest.
  • Forward signals. Stated strategy priorities coded to the same cell — announced intent that precedes grants by 12–24 months, each with a dated source.
  • Our fit. The CSBC-side read: how many of our 109 projects use the matching mechanisms, exemplar projects with honest outcome signals (including Not-tested and Dropped), and a short positioning read. This layer is our inference, not harvest data — it is labelled as such wherever it appears.

Five things the matrix says before you open a single card

    Who we looked at — 80 funders, split Indian vs global

    Data depth varies: . C-tier means only sector-level CSR disclosure exists — a visible gap is a finding, not a hole in the harvest.

    What we'd been missing — 13 newer / emerging funders now added

    The original harvest was built off Indian strategic philanthropy, the CSR Navigator, and the international funders already in our orbit. It under-weighted three fast-moving global spaces that have re-shaped in the last 12–18 months: the effective-giving / evidence funders (Coefficient Giving — the Nov-2025 rebrand of Open Philanthropy — GiveWell, EA Funds), the AI-and-behaviour funders (The Agency Fund, Cosmos Institute, Renaissance Philanthropy, the Humanity AI coalition), and the new climate-health vehicles (Quadrature, ClimateWorks' Adaptation & Resilience Fund, the COP30 Climate & Health Funders Coalition). They move fast, publish little in the CSR filings our harvest leaned on, and several are US/UK-domiciled — so a keyword-and-filings harvest was always going to miss them. They're now in the , flagged NEW.

    Verification discipline. Amounts are never estimated — empty means not public. Every grant carries a verification tag (verified / inferred / unconfirmed) and a source URL. 251 out-of-scope implementation grants are logged under their funders but excluded from all niche statistics. Anything in the "Our fit" panels is inferential and should not reach a funder-facing document without a pass from Pavan or Sharon.
    Rising themes

    What's become important, theme by theme

    The sector-first cut. Each theme opens into sub-themes matched by auditable keyword rules against every harvested grant purpose, forward signal and mirror finding — so "heat has become important within climate" is a claim you can click into and verify grant by grant. Grants can appear in more than one sub-theme where they genuinely straddle (a heat-and-gig-work grant counts in both); momentum compares 2024–26 grants against 2022–23.

    Each card carries: observed money (public amounts only — empty means undisclosed, not zero), the funder chase list with corpus signals quoted from their own strategy text, forward signals, the full grant record, peer precedent from the mirror pass, and our pitch read — the one inferential layer, flagged amber.

    What we've actually asked for — and who we're talking to

    This is the BD tracker read against the demand map: every proposal we've submitted since 2023 (won, lost, awaiting, in conversation) and every live funder relationship, with the contact, the stage, the ask and the follow-up. Where a funder here also appears in the harvest or in the new set, its name links across. Budgets shown are as-submitted; USD totals below sum only the USD-denominated asks.

    How to read a loss

    Most losses here carry no funder feedback — that's logged honestly rather than back-filled. Where we do have a reason, it clusters into two patterns worth naming: funders asking us to start smaller to build trust (the two 2024 BRAC WEE-DiFine asks, later re-won at $50k scale), and reviewers wanting a clearer mechanism-and-scale story (J-PAL SARWA, IPA DFS grievance). Both map onto the atlas's own advice: lead with mechanism, size the first ask to the relationship.

    Method & caveats

    What this is built from, and where it can mislead

    Everything here regenerates mechanically from five harvest files plus our own project database. Nothing on screen is generated from model knowledge — with one labelled exception.

    Pipeline

    • Track A (forward strategy): strategy pages, RFPs, annual letters, leadership statements — coded to mechanism × approach cells as strategy signals (305 rows, each dated and sourced).
    • Track B (backward harvest): individual grants, last 36–60 months preferred (737 rows). In-scope = research, evaluation, diagnostics, advisory, pilots with learning agendas, capability building, evidence-to-policy. Out-of-scope implementation (251 rows) is logged but excluded from niches.
    • Mirror pass: peer organisations checked for acknowledgements of each funder — now 185 findings, after adding CEGIS, IDinsight, Artha Global and Swaniti.
    • Aggregation: a niche = one (mechanism × approach) cell; momentum compares 2024–26 grant counts against 2022–23; value confidence = share of in-cell grants that are verified with a public amount.
    • CSBC-fit layer (the labelled exception): mechanism families are mapped to our project database's mechanism vocabulary (e.g. trust_calibration ← "Trust / credibility" + "Messenger effects"); project counts and exemplars are mechanical, but the positioning reads are our inference drawing on the evidence gap map v2 — flagged inferential on every card.

    Momentum — "entering" vs "exiting", in full

    • Entering.
    • Exiting.
    • Steady.
    • Thin data.

    Known limits. Amounts are missing wherever funders don't publish them (Wellcome and CIFF pages rarely carry GBP/USD figures) — empty is honest, not zero. Data-quality tiers vary: 11 funders at grant level, 54 at programme level, 13 at sector level only. Funder strategy documents are lagging indicators, so novelty is structurally under-represented; treat strategy-only cells as the frontier evidence. Momentum with fewer than two dated grants reads "thin data", not a trend. And the coding itself — which mechanism family a grant belongs to — is a judgement call by the harvest agents; spot-check before any cell's story carries weight in a deck.
    What's been added since the first harvest. Thirteen newer / emerging funders (led by Coefficient Giving and The Agency Fund) are now in the Funders tab, flagged NEW and profiled from public sources rather than the grant harvest. Four peer organisations — CEGIS, IDinsight, Artha Global and Swaniti — have been added to the mirror set with verified funder links. And the whole BD tracker (79 proposals, 29 relationships) now sits in the Our-pipeline tab, cross-linked to funder profiles where names overlap. The new-funder and BD layers are curated, not mechanically harvested — treat their "fit" reads as inference, like the CSBC-fit layer.
